issues.description: Behavior change: empty base_image now resolves to python:3.12 instead of KFP default image
issues.detail: In backend/kale/pipeline.py, _set_base_image previously set self.base_image = '' which the comment explicitly says relies on the 'kfp default image'. Changing this to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE ('python:3.12') silently overrides the KFP default for every user who relied on the empty-string fallback (e.g., when not running inside a notebook pod or when the K8s API call fails). This is a backward-incompatible behavior change that may break existing pipelines depending on the KFP-managed default image. The comment immediately above the change is now stale/misleading.

issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant duplicated across Python and TypeScript with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The string 'python:3.12' now appears in at least four places: backend/kale/pipeline.py (DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE), backend/kale/templates/nb_function_template.jinja2 (still has the literal as a final fallback), labextension/src/lib/Commands.ts (catch-block fallback), and labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx (exported DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE). The whole point of the PR is to centralize this — yet three of the four call sites will silently drift if the Python constant changes. The TS side should rely exclusively on the RPC value, or at minimum the literal should be defined once in a shared constants module.

issues.description: Base Image input replaced with a modal button — regression in editing ergonomics and discoverability
issues.detail: The inline Input control for Base Image (visible, editable in place) was replaced by a small 'IMAGE' button that opens a dialog. This is a UX regression: more clicks to edit, the current value is no longer visible at a glance in the row, and the button label 'IMAGE' is uninformative (button text is 'IMAGE' while title is 'Base Image'). Additionally, the button is now disabled unless stepName is non-empty, which is a new constraint not present before — users may be confused why the control is dead. If the goal was just to display the default, the inline Input with the default as a placeholder (already possible) would have been less invasive.

issues.description: Base image now always rendered, even for non-step cells, changing inline metadata semantics
issues.detail:
InlineMetadata.createBaseImageText previously returned '' when baseImage was unset, so non-step cells rendered nothing. After the change it always returns a

with the effective default image, regardless of whether the cell is actually a step. This will display 'Base Image: python:3.12 (default)' on cells where base image is irrelevant, which is visual noise and arguably incorrect. The caller should gate on cellType === 'step' (as the editor side does) before rendering the base image text, or createBaseImageText should accept that signal.

issues.description: Local import of DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE inside get_default_base_image RPC handler is unnecessary and inconsistent
issues.detail: backend/kale/rpc/nb.py imports DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE inside the function body via `from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE`. There is no circular-import justification offered, and the surrounding file imports from kale.* at module scope. Move the import to the top of the file for consistency, easier static analysis, and to avoid repeated import cost per RPC call.

issues.description: Jinja template retains hardcoded 'python:3.12' fallback that defeats the new constant
issues.detail: In backend/kale/templates/nb_function_template.jinja2 the expression is `step.config.base_image or base_image or default_base_image`. Since default_base_image is now always passed from the compiler, the literal fallback was removed — good. But the TS export of DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12' and the Commands.ts catch-block fallback still hardcode the same string; if Python ever bumps the default these will silently disagree. Consider documenting that the literal must be kept in sync, or wiring TS exclusively through the RPC value.

issues.description: Button width style '5%' is fragile and likely visually wrong
issues.detail: The new Image button uses `style={{ width: '5%' }}`. Percentage width on a small label button inside a flex/inline layout often produces an oddly narrow or stretched control depending on parent width. Prefer a fixed min-width or let MUI Button size itself naturally.

issues.description: Reset button does not close-and-confirm semantics clearly; uses 'Ok' rather than 'Close'
issues.detail: The dialog has 'Reset to Default' (which clears baseImage and closes) and 'Ok' (which only closes). Since editing the Input already calls updateBaseImage on each change, 'Ok' is really just 'Close'. Naming it 'Ok' implies a commit step that does not exist and may confuse users into thinking edits aren't saved unless they click Ok.

issues.description: Stale comment in _set_base_image refers to 'kfp default image' after behavior change
issues.detail: The comment block above `self.base_image = DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE` still reads '# Use kfp default image'. After the change, we're no longer deferring to KFP's default — we're forcing python:3.12. Update the comment to reflect actual behavior.

issues.description: No tests added for new RPC endpoint or default-image fallback behavior
issues.detail: The diff adds a new RPC handler (nb.get_default_base_image) and changes a backend fallback path (_set_base_image), but no unit tests are included. A small test asserting the constant and a smoke test for the RPC would prevent silent regressions if the constant is ever moved or renamed.

dissents.topic: Should _set_base_image default to 'python:3.12' or remain empty string?

positions.position: Using DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE makes the runtime behavior match what the UI advertises as 'default', so users see one consistent value end-to-end. Empty-string was a hidden indirection that was hard to reason about.

Empty string deferred to KFP's own default-image resolution, which may differ from python:3.12 and is correct for users who relied on KFP-managed images. The change silently overrides that pathway and should at minimum be feature-flagged or called out in release notes.

dissents.topic: Inline Input vs Dialog-behind-button for editing base image

positions.position: The new dialog is a regression: one fewer click, one fewer indirection beats a discoverable button. Showing the default as a placeholder in the existing Input would have met the requirement with no UX cost.

The dialog gives room to show 'Default: …' alongside the input and a Reset action, which an inline cramped Input could not. The button approach scales better if more per-step settings get added later.

dissents.topic: Single source of truth for DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE

positions.position: The TS literal and Commands.ts fallback must be eliminated; rely entirely on the RPC and fail loudly if it cannot be fetched.
RPC failures during notebook init are real; a hardcoded TS fallback prevents the UI from breaking. The cost of keeping one string in sync across the boundary is small and explicit.

review.summary: The PR achieves its stated goal of surfacing the default base image in the cell metadata UI, but bundles in two non-obvious changes that warrant scrutiny. First, _set_base_image now forces 'python:3.12' where it previously deferred to KFP's own default-image resolution — a backward-incompatible runtime change that should be called out and ideally separated from the UI work. Second, the inline Base Image input was replaced with a dialog-behind-button, which is an ergonomics regression and introduces a stepName-required gate not present before. The 'single source of truth' goal is undermined by the literal 'python:3.12' still being duplicated in TypeScript (CellMetadataEditor.tsx export, Commands.ts catch-block). Smaller cleanups: gate inline base-image rendering on cell type, move the RPC import to module scope, fix the stale 'kfp default image' comment, rename 'Ok' to 'Close', and add tests for the new RPC and fallback path.
